recentItems.title: Israeli forces demolish residential building in occupied East Jerusalem
recentItems.description:
Israel's military has been demolishing a multi-storey residential building in occupied East Jerusalem.  
The military raided the town of at-Tur with bulldozers and military vehicles surrounding the area ahead of the demolition.
Israel says the building was constructed without a permit.
The United Nations says, in the past nine months, Israel has displaced more than 740 Palestinians from 365 demolished structures in occupied East Jerusalem.

Al Jazeera’s Nida Ibrahim reports from Ramallah, occupied West Bank.

recentItems.title: Saudi Arabia says three injured in Houthi attacks on Jazan and Najran airports
recentItems.description:
Police in Saudi Arabia say at least three people have been injured in attacks on two airports in the southwest.
The strikes in Jazan and Najran follow an escalation in fighting in neighbouring Yemen. 
Its Saudi-backed government has launched a counteroffensive to retake territory from the Ansar Allah Houthis.
Since then, Riyadh has stepped up air strikes in support of the military operation. 

Al Jazeera’s Yousef Mawry reports from Sanaa, Yemen.

recentItems.title: Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi briefly detained as India election protests mount
recentItems.description:
Police in the ⁠Indian capital have briefly detained opposition leader Rahul Gandhi, during a protest demanding the ⁠resignation of ⁠the chief ⁠election commissioner.
An alliance of India’s opposition parties is marching to the Election Commission Headquarters in New Delhi. 
Protesters are accusing its chief, Gyanesh Kumar, of manipulating votes. 
They say the commission’s revision of the voter rolls has removed millions of eligible voters to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s governing BJP.

Al Jazeera’s Neha Poonia reports from New Delhi, India.

recentItems.title: Russia and Ukraine escalate attacks as drones target Moscow and strikes hit Kharkiv
recentItems.description:
Russia and Ukraine have intensified attacks on each other, with large-scale drone strikes targeting Moscow and Russian attacks hitting several Ukrainian cities.

At least two people were killed and seven injured in the Moscow region, according to local authorities, after hundreds of Ukrainian drones were launched overnight. A fuel storage and distribution facility southeast of Moscow was also reportedly hit.

In Ukraine, authorities say Russian attacks killed at least six people and injured dozens in Kharkiv. Strikes also targeted Odesa, where two Ukrainian cargo vessels were destroyed, as well as bridges across the Dnipro River.

The escalation comes as both sides continue targeting infrastructure ahead of winter, while Ukraine has proposed another round of trilateral talks involving Russia and the United States.

Al Jazeera’s Dmitry Medvedenko reports from Moscow and Jonah Hull from Kyiv.

recentItems.title: ‘Deterrence through credibility’: Analysts on Mecca defence pact and Yemen conflict
recentItems.description:
Turkiye and Pakistan have agreed to rapidly deploy military forces to Saudi Arabia.
That's after the three countries activated deterrence measures under the Mecca joint defence pact, signed in August. 
Their defence ministers held a high-level emergency meeting to discuss the Yemen conflict. 

Nawaf Obaid, senior research fellow at King’s College London and former special adviser to Prince Turki Al Faisal, says the Houthi defences are collapsing as the Saudi-led coalition’s military campaign evolves.

Retired Major General Zahid Mahmood, defence and security analyst, says the Mecca defence pact is a defensive alliance aimed at building credible deterrence and regional stability.

recentItems.title: Ethiopian PM Abiy demands Red Sea access as tensions with neighbours rise
recentItems.description:
Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed says Ethiopia will work to secure access to the sea.
Tensions between landlocked Ethiopia and Eritrea, which lies on the Red Sea, have been escalating due to fighting in the region.
Last week, Ethiopia cut diplomatic ties with its neighbour.
Eritrea has expressed fears Ethiopia could seek access to its port of Assab by force. 
But Abiy says Ethiopia intends to pursue access peacefully.

Al Jazeera’s Malcolm Webb reports from Nairobi, Kenya.

recentItems.title: Trump says US pulled bombers from UK’s RAF Fairford due to security threats
recentItems.description:
President Trump says the US removed its bombers from a British air base due to a threat linked to Iran.  
Earlier, Secretary of State Marco Rubio had called the transfer a normal rotation. 
The UK government insists the RAF Fairford airbase, where the bombers were housed, is safe. 

Al Jazeera’s Kimberly Halkett reports from Washington, DC.
